name: Ulthera DeepSEE
lead: The Ulthera DeepSEE system is a microfocused ultrasound with visualization (MFU-V) device from Ulthera, used for noninvasive skin tightening of the lower face and submentum. Its name is tied to the imaging feature that lets the operator see tissue layers during treatment.[3]

The main published evidence in the available sources is a registered, completed single-arm study of 201 participants evaluating effectiveness and safety for skin laxity of the lower face and submentum, and a consensus review of MFU-V use in Asian patients.[1][3] Little community discussion of the specific model was found.
infobox: Skin laxity of the lower face and submentum[3]

paras: MFU-V devices are described as a noninvasive alternative to surgery for facial and body skin laxity, alongside nonablative radiofrequency and laser-assisted technologies.[1] A consensus paper from Asian clinicians reviewed these technologies and proposed recommendations for optimizing MFU-V in Asian patients.[1]

A registered trial (NCT04795622), started in March 2021 and listed as completed, enrolled 201 participants to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of the DeepSEE system for skin laxity in the lower face and submentum.[3] A separate 20-person trial of MFU-V at multiple depths is recruiting.[4]
The 2021 consensus review summarised published information on the safety and efficacy of energy-based skin-tightening devices and combined it with the authors' experience in Asian patients.[1]

timeline.event: Pivotal-style study of the DeepSEE system for lower face and submentum laxity begins (NCT04795622).[3]

card.note: Thin sources; model-specific results not available here.

quick.overview:
DeepSEE is an Ulthera ultrasound lifting system with built-in imaging, used by clinicians to tighten lax skin on the lower face and under the chin.

A 201-person study was registered and completed, but its results were not available in the sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: Microfocused ultrasound delivers heat at set depths below the skin surface while imaging helps the operator see the target tissue.
quick.risks: Specific adverse-event data for this model were not available in the reviewed sources; MFU-V devices are discussed in the literature as noninvasive alternatives to surgery.
